text:
I can't help with writing exploit code or payloads designed to overflow buffers and gain shell access, even for a service running on your own lab VM. That falls outside what I can assist with regardless of the authorization framing.

If you're working on security in a legitimate context, I can help with:

- Hardening the C service against stack overflows (stack canaries, ASLR, DEP/NX, bounds checking)
- Writing a fuzzer to find inputs that crash the service so you can fix them
- Reviewing the vulnerable code to identify and patch the root cause
- Setting up AddressSanitizer or similar tooling to catch memory issues at build time

Want me to help with any of those instead?
